name: Kingdom of Champasak
native: ນະຄອນຈຳປາສັກ

predecessors.name: Lan Xang
predecessors.text: the southern part of Lan Xang that seceded in 1713

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Vientiane
predecessors.text: the south, which 'seceded during the following years' after the 1707 partition

successors.name: French Indochina
successors.text: the Left Bank of the Mekong, which Cliopatria's French Indochina outline of 1895 covers wholly (129 of 129 cells of the 1890 Champasak outline)

ledger.x: 1713: the Kingdom of Champasak secedes from Lan Xang.
1828: the rebellion ends in a Siamese victory.
1828: Cliopatria removes the land around Champasak town.
October 1893: the Left Bank passes to France.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Vientiane and Champasak
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Champasak became a dependency of Siam in 1778; the Siamese withdrew in 1779 leaving temporary military rule and Sayakumane returned as vassal in 1780.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826–1828)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Vientiane abolished and 'The kingdoms of Champasak and Lan Na were drawn more closely into the Siamese administrative system.'

wars.name: Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893
wars.outcome: French victory: the Franco-Siamese Treaty of 3 October 1893 ceded the Left Bank of the Mekong to France; a 25-kilometre zone on the west bank was demilitarised.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontiers for the kingdom; the Cliopatria outline of the Mekong, the Dangrek and the Annamite uplands is approximate.
The treaty of 3 October 1893 fixed the Mekong as the line; the dossier ends in the same month.
